findings.issue: The Q < K row reverses the net change. When Q < K, the net change is forward: reactants are consumed and products are formed. “Products consumed, reactants formed” describes the net reverse change for Q > K. As written, both inequality rows give the same direction, and the Q < K cell contradicts the Full-credit answer.
findings.evidence: CED 7.7 states that Q < K gives net forward change toward products, Q > K gives net reverse change toward reactants, and Q = K corresponds to dynamic equilibrium.
